importance_ranking.reason: This is an architectural membrane structure — the structural shape (conical, dome, arch, sail), fabric colour, and installation quality are all communicated visually. Buyers scan listing images to identify the structural form before reading any text; wrong shape or poor installation photo results in an immediate skip.

Fabric material (PVC/HDPE/PTFE/ETFE), cover type (fixed vs retractable), fabric GSM, and frame material are non-interchangeable across project requirements — a hotel specifying PTFE cannot substitute PVC, and a retractable system is a fundamentally different product from a fixed canopy. Buyers use these specs to shortlist fabricators before any contact.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — the Indian tensile structure fabrication market is fragmented across regional specialists; buyers search by fabricator capability and portfolio, not brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a turnkey supply-and-install project; the fabricator's installation track record, portfolio of completed pool covers, geographic service reach, and structural engineering capability are evaluated during vendor selection. An unknown fabricator with matching specs is still a procurement risk.

Indian buyers are price-sensitive and compare per-sq-ft rates, but price is only comparable after spec equivalence is confirmed — PTFE and PVC covers carry very different price tiers. Final price is always negotiated post-site-survey; the listed per-sq-ft rate is a budget entry point, not a final quote.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote large commercial installations as a per-project lump sum after site survey — per sq ft must be shown to enable price comparison across listings. Modular panel variants also follow per sq ft convention.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft is the dominant unit across all observed Indian sellers, but some listings quote per project — without the unit shown, buyers cannot compare prices across listings and risk significant misreading of cost.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — PTFE, PVC-coated, and HDPE are non-interchangeable across durability, light transmission, fire rating, and price tiers, with PTFE commanding a substantially higher price than PVC or HDPE for the same covered area.

Retractable (motorised) vs fixed cover represents a completely different structural system and fabrication scope, with retractable systems commanding a large price premium and requiring different engineering expertise.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Commercial and resort pool buyers require the structure to meet site-specific wind load requirements; sellers need this to engineer the frame correctly and confirm structural compliance before quoting.

Hotel, resort, and public pool buyers face fire safety compliance requirements; DIN 4102 B1/M2 and equivalent standards are referenced by Indian sellers and are a procurement gate for commercial projects.

Buyers choosing between translucent and opaque membranes need this spec to assess pool ambience and natural heating — a primary differentiator between ETFE/PTFE premium membranes and standard PVC/HDPE covers.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Fabric type directly routes the RFQ to the right fabricator tier — sellers specialising in PTFE or ETFE premium membranes operate at a different price point and capability level than PVC or HDPE fabricators, and cannot substitute one for another.

Structural shape determines fabrication complexity and engineering requirements — a seller with conical tensile expertise may not fabricate dome or hypar structures, making shape a primary routing signal for seller response accuracy.

missing_important_specs.why_important: A seller cannot determine fabrication scope, structural system, or price without knowing whether the buyer wants a fixed canopy or a motorised retractable cover — these are fundamentally different products requiring different engineering and manufacturing capability.
